title: Decision matrix ruleset
description: Version 1 first-match policy over normalized System One answers and host-verified facts. Rules run in order and the first whose when is true wins. If none matches, default_action applies.
$comment: validateRuleset in decision-matrix-rules is the reference. It accepts exactly the documents this schema accepts, and also checks what JSON Schema cannot: rule ids are unique, every referenced threshold resolves after overrides, conditions nest at most 32 levels, and with open_gate_requires_facts the default holds and every rule with gate false requires a fact on every path through when.

$schema.description: Optional. Lets an editor find this schema. Ignored by the engine.

open_gate_requires_facts.description: When true, default_action.gate must be true, and every rule with gate false must require a fact predicate on every path through its when (a fact under all, or under every branch of any). Model answers can then only hold.

owner.description: Who owns this policy. Optional. A strict lint can require it when the ruleset can open the gate.

ticket.description: Ticket or change id that introduced the policy. Optional. A strict lint can require it when the ruleset can open the gate.

agreements.description: Model/fact pairs. When the decision would open the gate and a pair disagrees, the result becomes a hold. An agreement never opens the gate.

default_action.description: Applies when no rule matches. Set gate true when an unrecognized event must not proceed.

text.description: A string with at least one non-space character.

thresholds.description: Named numbers that conditions reference. A caller can override any of them for one evaluation.

operand.description: A number, a numeric string, a threshold name, {{thresholds.name}}, or {"threshold": "name"}.

label.description: A choice label, compared literally and case-sensitively. A number is read as its string form.

type.description: The output field action, for example hold, block, pass, or review.

target.description: Who or what handles it. May contain {{answers.<id>.<field>}}, {{thresholds.<name>}}, and {{facts.<path>}}.

reason.description: Why, for people. Same placeholders as target.

gate.description: True holds: automation must not proceed. False opens the gate. Defaults to false when omitted.

id.description: Unique within the ruleset. No spaces.

predicate.title: Question predicate
predicate.description: Compares one model answer. Several operators on one predicate must all hold. Choice operators (eq, neq, in, not_in) fit choice questions. Numeric operators (gte, gt, lte, lt) fit noul and score questions. Confidence operators fit choice and score.

not.description: A question is either a choice or a noul/score, so choice and numeric operators cannot share a predicate.

factValue.description: A literal compared strictly. A string is never a threshold name here.

factOrdered.description: A number, a threshold name, or an ISO-8601 instant with Z or a numeric offset. Date-only strings are not ordered. An instant is compared as epoch milliseconds, not as text, and is not coerced to or from a number.

factSchema.description: Declared types for fact paths. A missing fact and a value of the wrong type stay errors. required false still errors when a rule reads a missing fact.

factPredicate.title: Fact predicate
factPredicate.description: Reads a value the host verified, passed to evaluateRules separately from the answers and never sent to the server. A missing fact, or a value of the wrong type for the operator, is an evaluation error rather than false. eq, neq, in, and not_in need a scalar fact whose type matches an operand (or null). contains and not_contains need an array of scalars. gte, gt, lte, and lt need a finite number, or an ISO-8601 instant on both sides. A number is not coerced to an instant.

fact.description: A dotted path through nested objects, for example grant.privileged.

answerView.title: Normalized answer
answerView.description: The shape evaluateRules reads. decision-matrix-systemone produces it from a server response. Another host can produce the same shape from its own client.
